body:
Explicit execution policies can be discarded by `vm run`/`vm trace`, while `code run` can continue after failing to open a requested policy. Bind the parsed policy, reject open/read/parse failures before VM execution, and verify that the loaded VM holds the requested policy. No-policy defaults and existing Axion semantics are preserved.

Refreshes the production fix and regression matrix from #613 against current code. Historical audit reports and receipts remain in #613; they are not relabeled as new execution. This PR carries four files: CLI implementation, test, and current CMake registration.

**Stacked on #747** via `fix/ci-backlog-portability` at `64310c2c`. After #747 merges, retarget this PR to main and run hosted checks before acceptance. Current main-only workflow filters do not validate a stacked PR automatically.

Fresh local validation: macOS ARM64, AppleClang 21, CMake 4.3, Release/C++23, strict deterministic float ON; isolated build with local Asio/Benchmark sources, pinned GTest, TUI/examples OFF.

- Same 73-process real-CLI matrix against the unfixed parent: **138 failed checks**.
- Corrected CLI: **73 processes, zero failed checks**.
- Registered `t81_cli_execution_policy_test`: **1/1 pass**; `git diff --check`: pass.

The matrix covers VM run/trace and code run on source/bytecode; three supported option positions; valid, missing, malformed, empty and zero-budget policies; no-policy defaults; invalid placement/missing values; sentinel output and rejected-trace creation. Current raw local receipts are retained separately from #613's historical evidence.

Draft pending review and hosted Linux/Windows/macOS coverage. No full-suite or general security-proof claim. Does not alter policy models, public APIs, governance activation or research authorization.

### Parent refresh and validation — 2026-11-10
Current parent is #747 at b18075ad. All non-CMake patch blobs remain unchanged, and the policy registration is retained alongside the JIT timeout and new baseline-checker test. The preceding refresh passed the registered CLI policy test with 73 real processes, zero failed checks. All CLI/wrapper/checker registrations were verified again after the latest parent merge; this is not a new native Windows execution claim.
title: fix(cli): enforce explicitly requested execution policies
